# TIA-2026-001: CRM vendor support access from the US

| Kind | Status | Version | RoPA entry | Vendor review | Business owner | Next review |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EU transfer impact assessment | Draft | 0.1 | ROPA-0001 | Recommended | Head of Sales | 2027-10-18 |

**Decision:** Open. Provisional: Step 3 needs the vendor's government-access record (Q1)

**Method:** EDPB Recommendations 01/2020 (six steps) and 2021 SCCs Clause 14; CJEU C-311/18 (Schrems II)

This assessment proposes a decision. It authorizes no processing; only the privacy lead's recorded approval does.

EU customer contact data is hosted in Frankfurt, and the CRM vendor's US support team can access it remotely. The vendor isn't DPF-certified, so the transfer relies on SCCs Module 2.

**Open items:** 0 supplementary measures shown effective · 0 questions block launch · 1 blocks approval
**Launch:** blocked by A1 (law).

## Analysis

Storing CRM data in the US is a Chapter V transfer on SCCs Module 2, so Clause 14 requires this assessment. Whether FISA 702 reaches the vendor is unknown, and no measure is yet shown to work against it. Provisionally open; it leans toward proceeding with measures if the vendor's facts limit exposure.
